ctx.x: Then I went to Copenhagen and made a tour with a nice Danish trombone player, John Darville and his group. They were nice musicians and pals and we played Arhus, Holback and did a radio show. Then I went to Oslo, my first time in Norway, and played with a dixieland band, the Big Chief Jazz Band. All were very nice fellows and we had a ball and drank quite a bit. We played at the Dow Tow Key Club and did a T.V. I went back to Denmark. I saw my old friend Timmie Rosenkrantz and his wife Inez Cavanaugh. He had a…

Buddy Tate had been in Paris and in Europe for a concert tour. I asked him if he would be interested to make a record with me for Pathe-Marconi. He liked very much the idea but had difficulties with the manager who had brought him in Europe. Jean-Marie Monnestier who was against the idea. He told Buddy that if he made the record, Monnestier would not pay his fare back to the U.S.A. So until the last minute, we still did not know if he would be there for the recording. I did another recording for a British fellow who was trying to push a young British pianist named Mike Garret. I was told that Mike had been doing a lot of classical piano, was very talented and wanted to play jazz. We decided to record in Paris with Art Taylor on drums, Jean Francois Castoire on bass and Francois Guin, named "Frick" on trombone. We found out that Mike had never before played with an ensemble and didn't know the art of accompanying soloists. We did our best and called the album "Three Generations…
